capabilities.title: Chat CRUD

Browser/sidecar mode keeps the legacy routes.

capabilities.title: Legacy compatibility authority boundary (ARC-11)
capabilities.notes: M1 Wave 1 (ТЗ §14.2, ADR-0039): per-legacy-API authority map shipped as packages/legacy-compat/COMPATIBILITY.md and enforced by apps/server/test/legacyAuthority.spec.ts — legacy Express routers are confined to /api/plugins/{id}/... capabilities.title: Prompt pipeline: durable PromptPlan (history/character/lorebook/token budget)
capabilities.notes: Kernel pipeline (ТЗ §9.1–§9.2, Этап 2.6): every generation run builds an immutable PromptPlan (character/persona system blocks from the card incl. ext_json.personality, lorebook keyword activation with constant/selective rules, last 128 non-tool history messages, heuristic-v1 approximate token budget with response-room reservation and oldest-unpinned truncation recording every excluded message id), stores it in prompt_plans (schema migration 5) and passes the instruct-neutral message array to adapters via ProviderRequest.messages — the OpenAI adapter serializes it verbatim. generation.prompt.plan (app.read) serves the stored plan; stable PROMPT_PLAN_FAILED / PROMPT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND. Tests: 5 unit + 2 kernel integration + 1 adapter. Honest boundaries: approximate tokenizer (model-specific registry pending), instruct template rendering deferred, lorebook character-scoping awaits the lorebook cutover.

capabilities.title: Durable run/step journal + tool-call loop (waiting_for_tool)
capabilities.notes: Этап 2.7 (ТЗ §8.3): the kernel journals every generation step in generation_steps (migration 6: ALTER TABLE generation_runs ADD COLUMN pending_tool_call_json + generation_steps table, no rebuild) and streams generation.step events (provider_turn/tool_call/tool_result/final_commit). A provider turn emitting a tool call is validated against the declarative tool registry (capability + minimal JSON-Schema argument check) and durably transitions the run to waiting_for_tool — a DERIVED wire status from the pending marker (DB status stays streaming; the v3 CHECK is untouched). The kernel NEVER executes tools: the host performs the effect and submits generation.tool.result, which journals the tool_result step, clears the marker and resumes the provider turn with the assistant tool_calls + tool-role messages. Stable terminal codes: TOOL_NOT_FOUND / TOOL_ARGS_INVALID / TOOL_LOOP_LIMIT (8 calls max) / TOOL_RESULT_STALE (non-idempotent submission). M5 slice 4 adds CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE pre-negotiation (ТЗ §9.3): a run whose provider does not declare tool support fails with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE before any network request instead of silently degrading to a no-tools turn; new wire error code, kernel_capability_negotiation.rs (3 integration tests: honest providers.list declarations, fail-before-generate probe, tools-capable pass-through). Crash-at-wait: fresh lease survives a reopen and the result still resumes; expired lease → interrupted (retry-safe). Этап 2.8: waiting-run cancel/retry — generation.cancel finalizes cancelled itself for a waiting run (no live executor) and every terminal writer clears the pending marker; retry from a cancelled waiting run starts attempt 2; retry on a still-waiting run is GENERATION_RUN_STATE_CONFLICT. Tools register via Kernel::register_tool; generation.tools.list (app.read) serves the registry. Tests: 7 tools.rs unit + 2 fake unit + 2 adapter + 10 tool_loop.rs kernel integration + 1 providers_openai tool round trip + 1 storage migration test. Этап 2.9: desktop host Integrated — the packaged kernel smoke registers a tool and completes a full waiting_for_tool → tool.result round trip over the real Tauri host path (NEOTA_DESKTOP_SMOKE=1); the host seam KernelHost::register_tool was added, and both Tauri-local and remote-http stream pollers now close the consumer stream when a run durably waits (previously an unbounded poll loop). Honest boundary: JSON-Schema validation covers a documented subset (object/required/additionalProperties + scalar/array/object types); the full schema engine is a follow-up. Этап 2.10: the facade exposes `generation.tools.list` / `generation.tool.result` on every NeoBackend implementation (LocalBackend over the wire; LegacyBackend honest UnsupportedError — no legacy route; RemoteBackend over the SDK); the UI has no tool surface yet — tool UX (step rendering, waiting_for_tool state, result submission) is Этап 4.

capabilities.title: Generation workflow (stream, cancel, retry, keep, discard)
capabilities.notes: Durable run/event model in kernel; run/step + tool protocol is M2 (GEN-RUN 10A/10B). Desktop host Integrated: the packaged kernel smoke (NEOTA_DESKTOP_SMOKE=1, Этап 2.9/2.10 — a kernel smoke, not yet the packaged golden E2E of ТЗ §17.2 with fault injection/yield-resume) drives character → chat → message → generation.start → durable save over the real Tauri host path (shell → KernelHost envelope → kernel → SQLite). Этап 2.10: the UI send flow streams over the Product Wire in kernel mode (`chats.messages.create` + `generation.start` via LocalBackend, deltas/completed/failed mapped onto the streaming handler); the browser/sidecar path keeps the legacy SSE route; regeneration and frontend prompt interceptors remain legacy-only and surface an honest UnsupportedError on the kernel (kernel prompt pipeline owns the prompt; interceptors deferred to the plugin cutover).

capabilities.title: Content-addressed asset store (put/get/content/delete, avatar linkage)
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 5 remainder (ТЗ §5.1 AssetStore port, AGENTS.md §11/§12): canonical assets over Product Wire (73 ops total). assets.put publishes immutable bytes under a content-derived managed key <kind>/<sha256>[.<ext>] via the crash-safe neotavern_storage::assets publisher (temp-write + sync + atomic rename + registry INSERT, symlink-safe resolution, orphan GC) and is an idempotent re-import — identical bytes under the same kind return the existing record with deduplicated:true (AGENTS.md: import must not create duplicates). assets.get returns metadata, assets.content returns the ORIGINAL bytes base64 (never lossy; the 4 MiB wire response limit caps the servable size, larger assets are addressed by relativeKey through host transports), assets.delete removes the registry row first (orphan GC covers the file). Avatar linkage is now writable: characters.create/update accept avatarAssetId and the kernel verifies the asset exists (stable ASSET_NOT_FOUND). Thumbnail CACHE generation (AGENTS.md §12 rules 4-9) remains the web/legacy side — the canonical plane deliberately has no image codec dependency; the thumbnail key contract (<original hash>+<size>+<algorithm version>, never regenerating when the key is unchanged) is documented and tracked within slice 5 remainder. 5 kernel tests cover round-trip, dedupe, avatar linkage, delete->not-found and validation. M5 slice 7 remainder web: the NeoBackend facade gained the AssetsApi (get/content/put/del) — the last wire domain without a facade surface, so every Product Wire operation is now reachable through the typed facade (ТЗ §13.1). LocalBackend forwards over the kernel transport with request/response validation, RemoteBackend forwards over the ClientSdk, LegacyBackend throws UnsupportedError (the legacy plane has no assets route — avatars/backgrounds remain legacy-raw until their own cutover). Parity + validation tests (68 neobackend). M5 slice 6 (ADR-0046 waiver 8 assets part): the legacy converter now maps avatar ORIGINALS into the canonical store — characters.avatar URLs (`/api/v2/assets/avatars/<sha256>.<ext>` or the thumbnail variant) resolve to `<data-dir>/files/avatars/<sha256>.<ext>`, the file is published as a `avatar` asset via the crash-safe publisher inside the conversion transaction (neotavern_storage::assets::publish_asset_in_tx) and `characters.avatar_asset_id` is linked; a missing file or unrecognizable avatar string is reported as an orphan (never silently dropped), and pre-avatar legacy schemas contribute 0. The legacy avatar string itself is still not copied verbatim (ТЗ §34 avatar→asset). Storage tests: avatar conversion round-trip + missing-original orphan in the legacy suite. M5 slice 6 remainder data (ADR-0046 waiver 8 settings + branches parts): the legacy settings table (key → value JSON text) converts verbatim into kernel settings (alue_json), non-JSON values survive as JSON strings (fail-closed), ConversionReport.settings + committed migration report count them; branches are resolved as a documented limitation — messages.branch_id has no kernel equivalent, ALL messages (active and side branches) are preserved flattened into the chat sequence (no message data dropped; branch semantics not reproduced). M5 slice 6 remainder web (avatar display, ТЗ §13.1): the UI data plane gained `readAssetContentDataUrl` — the kernel plane resolves an `avatarAssetId`'s original bytes over `assets.content` into a `data:` URI (the legacy plane has no asset store and refuses honestly), and the legacy avatar-original route moved OUT of React components into the `avatarOriginalUrl` transport helper (components never build /api/v2 URLs). `CharacterSummary`/`Character` now carry the canonical `avatarAssetId` (translateCharacterSummary passes it through) and the character editor/viewer renders the kernel avatar through it — kernel avatars are visible in the UI once conversion links them. ui:api:check product sites 38 → 37 (CharacterManagementPanel −2 avatar-original sites, wireBridge +1 transport site). M5 slice 6 remainder web (avatar upload, ТЗ §34): the character editor uploads an avatar on the kernel plane — uploadCharacterAvatar publishes the file as an immutable vatar asset (ssets.put, content-addressed + idempotent, ~786 KiB wire request cap surfaces as a transport error) and links it via characters.update(avatarAssetId); updateCharacter forwards a non-null vatarAssetId, CharacterCreate/Update carry the additive optional field, and the legacy plane keeps the gallery upload path. SEC-02 waiver 4 (per-profile export scoping) is recorded delivered — schema v14/v15, profile-scoped export + verification, profiles.* ops + facade ProfilesApi.export(profileId).

capabilities.title: Character-card import (PNG/JSON, content-hash dedupe)
capabilities.notes: Этап 4.5 (M5 slice 31): canonical character-card import over Product Wire (89 ops total). The card file (SillyTavern-compatible V2 JSON, or a PNG carrying the chara tEXt chunk with base64-encoded JSON) is staged through assets.put (kind card, content-addressed, idempotent; the ~786 KiB wire request cap surfaces as a transport error — never a silent downgrade) and parsed by imports.character.card: sha256 of the original bytes deduplicates against characters.import_hash (schema migration 019, indexed) so re-running an import returns the existing character with created:false (AGENTS.md §11: import must not create duplicates). Card fields beyond the canonical columns (personality, scenario, first message, example dialogue, system prompt, post-history instructions, creator, character version, extensions and any unknown fields) survive verbatim under ext_json._card (AGENTS.md §11: unknown character card fields and extension metadata must not be lost); over-length scalar columns are truncated with an honest warning. PNG cards link the staged asset as the avatar (avatar_asset_id = asset id); JSON cards carry none. Missing asset → stable ASSET_NOT_FOUND; unparseable card → CHARACTER_CARD_INVALID with a reason param (INVALID_JSON/INVALID_PNG_SIGNATURE/TRUNCATED_PNG_CHUNK/INVALID_PNG_CARD_ENCODING/PNG_CARD_METADATA_MISSING). Kernel tests (kernel_imports.rs, 5): JSON create + field preservation, dedupe, PNG avatar link, unparseable reject, missing asset. Host parity (Этап 5 foundation): remote_http.rs character_card_import_over_http drives the full flow over the loopback HTTP adapter — assets.put -> imports.character.card -> created, re-import dedupe (created:false, same id), ASSET_NOT_FOUND and CHARACTER_CARD_INVALID (reason param) error envelopes verbatim, every payload wire-validated through the generated decoders. Facade: NeoBackend.imports.characterCard — LocalBackend forwards with request/response validation, RemoteBackend via ClientSdk, LegacyBackend throws UnsupportedError. Web transport: importCharacter on the kernel plane now runs assets.put + imports.character.card (two-step); UI wiring (CharactersPage/CharacterManagementPanel) is slice 32.

capabilities.title: Lorebook CRUD
capabilities.notes: M4 slice 1 (Этап 4.1): full lorebook CRUD + entry-level CRUD in the kernel through Product Wire. Book ops: lorebooks.get/create/update/delete joined lorebooks.list; entries travel as wire.lorebook.entry.input objects (keys/secondaryKeys/content/enabled/constant/selective) that the prompt pipeline already activates (constant always, keyword case-insensitive substring, selective primary+secondary), stored into entries_json with entryCount derived via json_array_length; the kernel owns per-entry id/position/metadata/timestamps so stored rows satisfy the portable ExportLoreEntry shape (export/import stay lossless). Entry ops (M4 follow-up closed): lorebooks.entries.list/create/update/delete — the kernel assigns the entry id and appends at the end on create, update is a partial patch (position/metadata/createdAt preserved), delete removes exactly one entry; stable product errors LOREBOOK_NOT_FOUND (lorebookId param) and LOREBOOK_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND (entryId param); strict unknown-field rejection. Tested at four levels: 2 kernel integration tests (entry CRUD round trip + error paths), wire corpus (4 new positive + 7 new negative fixtures, generated.rs regenerated), contracts-generated fuzz probes, and the remote-http host-parity test (lorebook_crud_over_http extended with the entry cycle). Desktop Integrated via the facade `apps/web/src/api/wireBridge.ts`: the entry hooks route through the wire ops in kernel mode with honest wire→UI translation (the wire DTO has no position/metadata, so the UI receives neutral defaults and an explicit position/metadata patch is CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE); legacy /api/v2 keeps the nested route for sidecar mode. M5 slice 6 closes ADR-0047 waiver 2 (character↔lorebook scoping): schema migration 016 adds the STRICT `character_lorebooks` link (one optional owner per book — a book is either shared-library or bound to exactly one character); LorebookDto.characterId (optional uuid) is bound at create/update (unknown character → CHARACTER_NOT_FOUND) and reported by get/list; lorebooks.list accepts an optional characterId filter (shared-library books still list without it); prompt retrieval is scoped by the chat's character via the link while books without a link stay global; the legacy converter maps `lorebooks.metadata.characterId` into the canonical link (a link to a character that did not survive conversion is reported as an orphan and the book stays shared). Facade cutover (M5 slice 6 remainder web): the NeoBackend LorebooksApi.list accepts the scoped request (LocalBackend/RemoteBackend forward it — parity-tested; LegacyBackend UnsupportedError) and wireBridge stops throwing CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE for scoped catalogs. Honest boundary: legacy /api/v2/lorebooks route removal remains Этап 4.

capabilities.title: Memory CRUD (ТЗ §4.4)
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 3: memory CRUD in the kernel through Product Wire (memories.list/create/update/delete) backed by the STRICT memories table with scope/keys/content/enabled/position/metadata (schema migration 9). Character-scoped create requires characterId (unknown character → CHARACTER_NOT_FOUND); list filters scope/characterId/enabled and orders by position, created_at, id. Legacy→kernel migration maps the memories table (scope validated, dangling character_id preserved — no FK by design). Facade: NeoBackend.memories + LegacyBackend over /api/v2/memories + web hooks (useMemories/useCreateMemory/useUpdateMemory/useDeleteMemory) route through the wire ops in kernel mode. Prompt integration (same slice): the kernel prompt plan injects keyword-activated memory blocks scoped to the chat's character as source:'memory' system blocks (honest memory-keyword-v1 heuristic — the kernel has no FTS yet; memories_fts is not converted; semantic/vector retrieval stays a later slice). The memory settings editor UI (MemoryEditor tab in AI settings) delivers CRUD: content/keys/scope/character picker/enabled toggle + delete confirm (component tests 2/2). Honest boundaries: the wire DTO cannot express `characterId: null` (un-scoping is CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE).

capabilities.title: Kernel handshake / meta
capabilities.notes: Exact local handshake (schemaHash + FFI ABI) enforced at kernel open; exercised by desktop smoke and JNI bridge. Slice 7 part 1 (M5): the web transport maps meta.get onto the legacy VersionResponse (appVersion -> version, api.major -> apiVersion; the static product name is identity, the UI renders only the version string) and useAppVersion routes through the transport — the HomePage version label now reads the kernel on the kernel plane.

capabilities.title: Persona CRUD
capabilities.notes: M4 slice 1 (Этап 4.1, ТЗ §8.1 Library context): full persona CRUD in the kernel through Product Wire (personas.list/get/create/update/delete) backed by the STRICT personas table (schema migration 7). The single-default invariant matches the legacy PersonaRepository: create/update with isDefault clears the previous default in the same transaction. Wire DTO wire.persona.dto carries name/description/avatar/isDefault/createdAt/updatedAt (description/avatar optional); stable PERSONA_NOT_FOUND with personaId param. Tested at three levels: 2 kernel integration tests (round trip incl. default demotion + NOT_FOUND/contract paths), wire corpus (4 positive + 5 negative fixtures), and a remote-http host-parity test (persona_crud_over_http). Desktop Integrated via the facade `apps/web/src/api/wireBridge.ts`: the persona hooks (usePersonas/useCreatePersona/useUpdatePersona/useDeletePersona) route through the wire ops in kernel mode with honest wire→UI translation (avatar null default); an explicit avatar clear (avatar: null) is not expressible in the wire contract and surfaces CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, never a silent no-op. Legacy→kernel migration carries the personas table (audit P0 #3 fix) with the single-default invariant enforced on insert; sources without the table contribute 0. Этап 4 slice 3 closes the persona-application waiver (ADR-0047 waiver 3): chats.create/chats.update carry personaId (PERSONA_NOT_FOUND, ON DELETE SET NULL) and the prompt pipeline resolves the chat persona name into the plan `userName`, substituting it for the {{user}} macro across the selected history and the current input (kernel tests kernel_persona_application: chat linkage round trip + plan substitution + verbatim pass-through without a persona). Honest boundary: the kernel has no global active-persona fallback — a chat without a persona_id renders no {{user}} substitution (legacy resolveActive(chat, appSettings) fallback is a legacy-server behavior, documented); legacy /api/v2/personas route removal remains Этап 4.

capabilities.title: Preset CRUD
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 3: full preset CRUD in the kernel through Product Wire (presets.list/get/create/update/delete) backed by the STRICT presets table with kind (schema migration 9). The legacy kind pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` is part of the wire contract; duplicate (kind,name) → stable PRESET_CONFLICT (Conflict class) pre-checked outside the transaction. Presets are created with kind; the pre-existing legacy presets rows (kind from the source table, name/data/settings_json) convert in the legacy→kernel migration. Desktop Integrated via the facade `apps/web/src/api/wireBridge.ts`: the preset hooks (usePresets/useCreatePreset/useUpdatePreset/useDeletePreset) route through the wire ops in kernel mode with honest wire→UI translation (RFC 3339 → epoch-ms), powering the existing GenerationPresetEditor and PromptTemplateEditor panels; browser/sidecar mode keeps the legacy /api/v2/presets routes via LegacyBackend (ms timestamps mapped to RFC 3339). Honest boundary: preset data is opaque JSON — no per-field validation beyond the wire size limits.

capabilities.title: Provider configuration (secrets out of the DB)
capabilities.notes: Kernel-owned ops with component tests (ТЗ §9.4, Этап 2.4): provider_configs rows hold non-secret config_json plus an opaque secret_ref; the API key is stored through the kernel's SecretStore seam (Kernel::set_secret_store) and never reaches the DB, the wire DTO, backups or diagnostics — get/list report only hasApiKey. Without a wired store, set with apiKey fails SECRET_UNAVAILABLE (fail-closed); delete revokes the stored secret. Hosts wire real SecretStore backends in M3 (OS vault / Keystore / portable).

capabilities.title: Provider catalog read
capabilities.notes: Kernel op exists; provider configuration without secrets in DB is delivered (providers.config.*). M5 slice 4: every provider DTO now carries the adapter's honest capability declaration (wire.provider.capabilities: tools/vision/thinking/jsonMode/streaming) so the UI can pre-negotiate without guessing; the kernel generation path enforces the same declaration — a run that would send tool calls to a provider without tool support fails with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE before any network request (kernel_capability_negotiation.rs proves generate is never invoked).

capabilities.title: OpenAI-compatible production provider
capabilities.notes: Adapter crate (ТЗ §9.3, Этап 2.5) with 14 unit + 4 kernel integration tests: chat-completions streaming over a minimal blocking HTTP/1.1 client with rustls TLS (OS trust store), bounded SSE reads (SEC-04), normalized errors. API key resolved at execution time from the config's secret_ref through the SecretResolver seam (Kernel::set_secret_resolver) and passed via ProviderRequest::api_key — only in the Authorization header, never in body/DB/logs; missing resolver fails closed. Registration via the new Kernel::register_provider seam; config instance selection in the run model. Этап 2.7: serializes declared tools (function schema) and the resumed-turn tool context (assistant tool_calls + tool-role result), accumulates SSE tool_calls deltas into normalized ProviderEvent::ToolCall. Этап 2.8: kernel integration test drives the full tool round trip over the real SSE path — turn 1 streams a normalized tool call, the kernel validates and durably waits, generation.tool.result resumes turn 2 with the tool context, the run completes with exactly one assistant message; both HTTP bodies are asserted (tools serialization + resumed tool_call_id). M5 slice 4: the adapter declares its honest capabilities (tools/streaming true; vision/thinking/jsonMode false — no silent downgrade) via the new ProviderAdapter::capabilities port method; wire.provider.capabilities surfaces it in providers.list. The Anthropic adapter remains the documented TS-side SDK exception (packages/provider-sdk), legacy contour — the canonical plane has no Rust Anthropic adapter yet, and capability declaration makes that absence honest at the list surface.

capabilities.title: Plugin network broker (SSRF policy + bounded streaming)
capabilities.notes: SEC-03/SEC-04 (M1 Wave 1 + Wave 2 + Wave 3): plugin network.http.fetch and socket destinations pass the §29.1 SSRF scope policy — every DNS answer checked, bracketed IPv6 and IPv4-mapped literals normalized, per-hop redirect re-checks, connect to the policy-approved IP with the hostname only in Host/SNI and post-connect remoteAddress verification; response bodies are capped while streaming and the connection is destroyed on exceed (apps/plugin-runtime/src/host). Wave 2 (SEC-04): global and per-plugin in-flight byte budgets (NETWORK_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES_GLOBAL=64 MiB, NETWORK_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES_PER_PLUGIN=16 MiB, worst-case reservation per fetch body NETWORK_MAX_BODY_BYTES) fail a NEW request with the stable NETWORK_INFLIGHT_LIMIT before its body is read, and release on success/error/cancel; two host tests cover both budgets (including a cross-plugin global trip with 8 concurrent held fetches). Wave 3 (SEC-03): the verified-IP set is now honored on EVERY connect — direct fetch, HTTP absolute-form proxy hops (verified IP in the request-target, Host keeps the hostname), HTTPS CONNECT tunnels (verified IP in the CONNECT authority, TLS validates the hostname), tcpConnect, udpSend AND WebSocket (the undici WebSocket was replaced by a socketHandles RFC 6455 client that connects to a policy-approved address, verifies remoteAddress after connect and performs the HTTP Upgrade itself — no DNS for the hostname in the stack).

capabilities.title: Plugin package trust (signature/digest verification)
capabilities.notes: SEC-05 (M1 Wave 1): publisher Ed25519 signature + per-file sha256 digest verification before consent/install (format neotavern.package-signature.v1, apps/server/src/lib/packageTrust.ts); trust states built-in / verified-publisher / locally-trusted / unsigned-untrusted recorded in the plugin registry (migration 0023) and surfaced as InstalledPlugin.trust; NEOTA_PLUGIN_PUBLISHER_KEYS keyring + NEOTA_PLUGIN_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE policy; unsigned packages enabled via consent become locally-trusted; ZIP/tar.gz reject duplicate normalized paths, symlinks, traversal, encrypted entries and bounded zip bombs.

capabilities.title: Restore maintenance lock (global maintenance mode)
capabilities.notes: M1 Wave 1 (ТЗ §10.4): restore runs exclusively under a global maintenance lock (apps/server/src/lib/maintenance.ts) — while held, new product mutations are rejected with the stable MAINTENANCE_MODE error (503), plugin activation is blocked and no second restore can enter; read-only requests and backup/diagnostics tooling keep working; the lock is released on every exit path (success and failure). Full stop-the-world (suspending in-flight generations, staged data-root activation) is the M3 DATA-ACTIVATE slice.

capabilities.title: SecretStore (secrets out of the main DB, portable secrets.enc)
capabilities.notes: SEC-01 (M1 Wave 1): new SecretStore port package (packages/secret-store) with three explicit backends — portable encrypted secrets.enc (AES-256-GCM, versioned scrypt KDF, authenticated header, atomic writes, fresh nonce per write, machine-independent key derivation, lock/re-encrypt), session-only memory (no plaintext fallback) and a read-only env provider for headless (NEOTA_SECRET_*). Provider and plugin secrets no longer live in app.db: migration 0024 adds value_ref columns and the DB stores only opaque references (portable:/session:/env:), resolved at runtime via ctx.secrets (apps/server/src/lib/secretStore.ts, migration 0024). Pre-migration plaintext rows are imported at bootstrap (idempotent). A reference whose backend cannot produce the value surfaces SECRET_UNAVAILABLE_ON_THIS_DEVICE (422) — never a plaintext fallback; backups and profile exports contain no secrets. Kernel-plane port delivered (crates/secret-store, ADR-0040): canonical portable v2 format with Argon2id (m=64 MiB/t=3/p=1) + AES-256-GCM, authenticated header, staged re-encryption, cross-machine portability tests (15 tests). OS-vault / Android Keystore adapters and the full portable UX (passphrase prompt, auto-lock UI) remain M3.

capabilities.title: Non-secret settings (kernel)
capabilities.notes: M5 slice 7 (Этап 4.7, ТЗ §8.1 Configuration): canonical key → JSON-object settings store backed by the STRICT settings table (schema migration 11). settings.update is a transactional upsert returning the post-update snapshot; settings.get reads a key subset or the full snapshot. Secrets never live here — provider keys are in the SecretStore (ТЗ §9.4, SEC-01); the wire DTO carries object values only (scalar preferences wrapped at the UI boundary). Slice 7 part 2 (M5): the web transport maps the typed AppSettings projection onto the wire store — camelCase fields to wire-valid kebab keys (maxContextTokens -> max-context-tokens, extensions.legacyFrontend -> extensions.legacy-frontend), scalar preferences round-trip in { value: X } form, post-update snapshot contract preserved; settings.get wraps non-object stored values (legacy bare scalars) and the legacy converter normalizes camelCase settings keys to kebab form, so converted stores stay wire-readable. useSettings/useUpdateSettings (and the AutoConnectSync last-server/auto-connect writes) now route through the transport.

capabilities.title: Diagnostics panel (kernel section)
capabilities.notes: First vertical slice through the NeoBackend facade; legacy sections remain on /api/v2 until M4. Delivered in M1a (Wave 0 Governance). M5 slice 7 (Этап 4.7, ТЗ §15, SEC-07): canonical diagnostics.export builds a redacted ALLOWLIST bundle — versions (app/wire/schema hash + revision + storage format + SQLite), setting count and generation-run counters (total/completed/failed/waiting), pinned redaction: 'allowlist'. Provider configs, secret refs, setting values and message content are never read (structural redaction, fail-closed by omission); kernel tests prove a sentinel secret and message token never reach the bundle. M5 slice 9 (Этап 4.4/4.7): AutoConnectSync no longer uses legacyRaw — the model warm-up routes through wireBridge warmProviderModels (kernel: honest UnsupportedError, model discovery has no wire op yet); the diagnostics panel maps the kernel SEC-07 bundle honestly (schema rev + hash, storage format, SQLite version, settings count, generation runs) and disables legacy-sidecar search/cache maintenance in kernel mode with an explicit explanation — no fabricated legacy fields. M5 slice 10 (Этап 4.5): the legacy bridge sendChatMessage routes through the transport — kernel plane creates via wire chats.messages.create and returns the lean MessageDto projected onto the documented BridgeChatMessage surface (createdAt RFC3339 on kernel vs epoch-ms on legacy; never fabricated), legacy plane keeps the full legacy message.

Slice 11 (M5): wire chats.messages.update gains optional content + meta (free-object), MessageDto carries meta verbatim; toggleMessageContext / swipeGreeting / deleteCheckpoint now route through updateChatMessage on both planes (ui-legacy-surface 60 → 57). Slice 13 (M5): ChatPage checkpoint/branch creation routes through the transport (ui-legacy-surface 57 → 56, last legacyRaw removed from ChatPage). Slice 14 (M5): kernel chats.snapshots.create owns the snapshot capability on the kernel plane — checkpoint/branch children carry parentChatId/origin/sourceMessageId, open-checkpoint reads MessageDto.checkpointChatId, deleteCheckpoint clears the real link via clearCheckpointChatId (ui-legacy-surface 56 → 54); the legacy contour keeps its full snapshot flow on the sidecar/webClient planes.

capabilities.title: Plugin management UI
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 6 part 1 (M5): canonical Extensions-context registry over Product Wire (78 ops total) — schema v12 STRICT plugins table + 5 ops. The kernel durably records what the host ALREADY verified (SEC-05: publisher Ed25519 signature + per-file digest + ZIP traversal/symlink/bomb rejection stays in the legacy host packageTrust.ts) and what the user consented to: version, trust state (built-in / verified-publisher / locally-trusted / unsigned-untrusted), publisher key fingerprint and the GRANTED permission set — the install/update request IS the consent moment (ARC-08). Fail-closed: an install that would LOWER the recorded trust rank is rejected (stable PLUGIN_TRUST_DOWNGRADE product code — an unsigned package can never silently replace a verified one), same id+version re-install is idempotent, enable/disable are idempotent flag transitions, uninstall of an unknown plugin is PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND. The table holds NO code, NO secrets and NO runtime handles — execution and cleanup (SEC-06) live in the isolated host executor behind the versioned capability protocol (ТЗ §14.1); themes (Theme SDK registry) and the legacy ST v1 translation remain slice 6 parts 2-3. 4 kernel tests cover the round trip, idempotent re-install, trust-downgrade rejection and wire validation. Slice 6 part 4 (M5): the web transport now calls the wire plugins ops — readPlugins/activatePlugin/disablePlugin/deletePlugin map the durable record (trust state + granted permission set fixed at the install consent moment) onto the legacy InstalledPlugin shape with honest neutral fields for what the wire row does not model (apiVersion 1 = does not advertise a higher SDK, has* surfaces false = not declared, compatibilityLevel native-v3); activation applies the RECORDED permissions and refuses a different requested set (CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE) instead of silently enabling with different rights; flows needing the host package verifier or the plugin executor (package install, git install, runtime safe mode, OAuth auth connections) are honest refusals — never a silent skip of SEC-05 verification or SEC-06 cleanup. safeMode is honestly false on the kernel plane (no kernel safe-mode mechanism). All 10 plugin hooks route through the transport. ui:api:check stays 64 sites (plugin routes were already parameterized through the client base).

capabilities.title: Portable data / activation / restore
capabilities.notes: M3 (ADR-0041): versioned data roots (roots/root-<id>/ + active-root.json pointer), durable activation journal with prepared/validated/activation_pending/committed/rolled_back statuses, and the Windows restart-to-complete protocol (bounded transient retry, activation_pending after budget, resolve at open) implemented in neotavern_storage::activation with 21 integration tests; v1 flat layout still fully supported. The staged legacy→kernel migration in the application flow (neotavern_storage::migration: lease-locked preflight incl. disk space, verified pre-migration-* safety copy, convert into a staging versioned root, FK/current-revision validation, report, journaled commit with bounded retry, idempotent re-run, cancel-before-activation) is implemented with 19 integration tests. The migration corpus (ТЗ §17.4) covers: all released schema revisions 1..6 upgrade, future schema fails closed, corrupted DB detected, interrupted migration recovers, the REAL Drizzle layout maps completely (card fields personality/scenario/first_message/example_dialogues/system_prompt/post_history_instructions/creator/creator_notes survive into ext_json; character_tags/tags join merged into tags_json; unknown ext preserved; soft-deleted rows skipped and reported), a 1000x1000x3000 library converts with exact counts, unicode/RTL/20k-char values round-trip, and the Windows platform corpus holds a real handle without FILE_SHARE_DELETE: pointer switch exhausts the bounded retry budget, commit returns the stable recoverable ActivationPending, the next open resolves it (restart-to-complete). The CLI host flow (neotavern-cli --migrate-legacy, Этап 3 work 7-8) runs the offline converter with the kernel closed, then opens the kernel on the activated root — the canonical data-root switch is verified by product reads (13 CLI E2E tests incl. characters.get round-trip on the versioned root). Remaining Этап 3 slice: upgrade drills on packaged Windows/macOS/Linux artifacts. The upgrade drill (scripts/upgrade-drill.mjs, Этап 3 work 7) proves the cross-platform upgrade cycle on the real CLI artifact: a Drizzle-style fixture converts, characters.get returns the migrated character, the legacy database stays byte-identical (immutable source, ТЗ §10.3), re-running the migration is idempotent (one committed entry, one staging root), the pre-migration safety copy matches the source checksum, and the journal ends committed with the rollback pointer retained. PASS on Windows in this session; macOS/Linux runs gate the release branch in CI (Windows lock-contention/restart-to-complete stays covered by the Rust held-handle test). M5 slice 7 adds the canonical-plane surface for the portable secrets half: secrets.status reports kind 'portable' with the secrets.enc formatVersion when a FileEncryptedSecretStore is wired (SEC-01.1 — the UI distinguishes portable-encrypted from machine-bound/session-only/unavailable and never sees a value).

capabilities.title: Logical profile export
capabilities.notes: SEC-02: legacy export (apps/server/src/lib/profileExport.ts) implemented in M1 Wave 1 and hardened in Wave 2 - logical allowlist archive (format v2, snapshot transaction, explicit column allowlist verified via PRAGMA table_info, sentinel negative tests). M5 slice 5 adds the canonical-plane op profile.export over Product Wire: the kernel builds a fresh verified container under the data root's exports/ (characters/chats/messages/lorebooks/presets + optional assets via storage create_export/verify_export) and returns the verified report; provider configs and secrets are not export sections by construction and the kernel negative test proves a sentinel SecretStore value never reaches any container byte. M5 slice 5 remainder (ADR-0047 waiver 4) adds per-profile scoping: schema v15 binds characters to profiles (profile_id FK, ON DELETE SET NULL) and profile.export accepts an optional profileId — the scoped container carries only that profile's characters and, transitively, their chats/messages (lorebooks/presets are the shared library, always included in full); the manifest records the scope and an unknown profile id is PROFILE_NOT_FOUND. Scoped export round-trips through import: a binding is preserved only when the profile already exists in the target, otherwise the character lands unassigned and is reported — data is never dropped for a missing binding (storage export tests + kernel_profile_export). UI/facade cutover (M5 slice 5 remainder web): the NeoBackend facade exposes profile.export (LocalBackend/RemoteBackend forward, LegacyBackend UnsupportedError — parity-tested) and the Settings Profiles tab offers a per-profile scoped export action wired through useProfileExport, reporting the per-section counts; secrets still never enter the container.

capabilities.title: Profiles (Configuration)
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 5 remainder part 2 (M5): canonical Configuration bounded context (ТЗ §8.1) over Product Wire — schema v14 STRICT profiles table + 4 ops, then schema v15 per-profile binding (characters.profile_id FK, ON DELETE SET NULL). The NeoBackend facade exposes profiles.list/create/rename/del (LocalBackend forwards over the kernel transport, RemoteBackend over ClientSdk, LegacyBackend throws UnsupportedError for all four); the Settings panel gained a Profiles tab (list, create, rename, delete with confirm) wired through TanStack Query hooks, with a per-profile scoped export action that calls profile.export (SEC-02, ADR-0047 waiver 4; op owned by ui.profile-export). kernel_profiles tests (3), facade parity tests (profiles + profile.export), ProfilesPanel component tests (4).

capabilities.title: Secret management
capabilities.notes: SEC-01: backend SecretStore + portable secrets.enc delivered in the legacy contour (M1, see security.secret-store); OS vault / Keystore adapters remain M3; no reveal op by design. M5 slice 7 adds the canonical-plane value-free surface secrets.status (ТЗ §SEC-01.1): it reports the explicit mode — kind 'portable' (encrypted secrets.enc with formatVersion), 'env', 'session' (session-only) or 'unavailable' — plus persistent/writable/available flags and the record count, WITHOUT ever invoking get (a value cannot cross this DTO; the kernel test plants a sentinel in a session and a portable store and proves it never appears in the response bytes). M5 slice 7 remainder web: the Settings panel gained a Security tab (SecretsPanel) rendering the honest mode state (portable encrypted / machine-bound / session-only / fail-closed unavailable) plus persistent/writable/available flags, record count and portable format version from the DTO via the NeoBackend facade (LocalBackend/RemoteBackend forward, LegacyBackend UnsupportedError), wired through useSecretsStatus; the panel explicitly states there is no reveal operation. SecretsPanel component tests (2); the passphrase-entry and auto-lock UX remain the web facade.

capabilities.title: Themes
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 6 part 2 (M5): canonical Theme-SDK registry over Product Wire (82 ops total) — schema v13 STRICT themes table + 4 ops. A theme is DATA, never code: opaque manifest + content-addressed CSS asset reference (cssAssetId published via assets.put kind theme-css, existence validated at install — the table holds no CSS bytes, no chats access, no keys, AGENTS.md §19). Single active flag names the applied theme; uninstalling the ACTIVE theme clears it so the shell falls back to the default (a broken theme must never block interface reset). Fail-closed mirrors plugins: version change that would LOWER the recorded SEC-05 trust rank is rejected (stable THEME_TRUST_DOWNGRADE product code), same id+version re-install idempotent, install never activates (activation is an explicit consent), unknown uninstall/activate is THEME_NOT_FOUND. Legacy theme routes + theme SDK v1 translation remain slice 6 part 3. 5 kernel tests (kernel_themes.rs). Slice 6 part 3 (M5): the web transport now calls the wire themes ops — readThemes/activateTheme/deleteTheme map the durable theme row onto InstalledTheme (CSS asset resolved to a data: URI through the existing assets.content path, honest no-CSS fallback when the read fails or exceeds the 262 144-byte content cap), and the remaining UI theme surface moved out of components: theme settings (readThemeSettings) and the user stylesheet (userCssUrl) are transport helpers (kernel plane honestly reports none — the wire contract does not model theme settings or a user.css service yet). Honest CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE remains where the wire contract cannot express the legacy flow: theme-package install (host-side SEC-05 verification must precede themes.install — no such host command exists in the web transport). Slice 6 part 5 (M5 slice 18): new wire op themes.deactivate (87 ops total) — the explicit 'stop applying a theme' consent (clears the single active flag, idempotent: no active theme is a successful no-op; the shell falls back to the default), distinct from uninstall which also removes the row. The web resetActiveTheme kernel branch now calls the op instead of UnsupportedError; the legacy contour keeps DELETE /themes/active. 6 kernel tests (kernel_themes.rs), wire.test 88 ops, neobackend 69/69.

capabilities.title: Character card / chat exports & character import (legacy containers)
capabilities.notes: SillyTavern card containers (PNG/JSON card export, chat snapshot export, card import parsing) have no wire operation — the kernel plane refuses them honestly (M5 slice 8: exportCharacterCard/exportChat throw UnsupportedError on the kernel plane and keep the legacy download on the legacy plane; useErrorText localizes the refusal via errors:UNSUPPORTED instead of INTERNAL. M5 slice 32: character-card IMPORT now runs on the kernel plane end-to-end — assets.put + imports.character.card (Этап 4.5) — so the remaining refusals are the two EXPORT directions, which the wire contract does not model). The legacy /api/v2/characters/:id/export, /api/v2/chats/:id/export and /characters/import routes stay the implemented surface until a canonical container/parse operation is specified (ТЗ §14.2 authority-non-expanding boundary).
